name: Anavar / oxandrolone voice risk

card.summary: Mild-reputation oral steroid whose documented risks in women include voice deepening that can be irreversible.
card.note: Virilization in women can be permanent; FDA approval withdrawn 2023.

quick.overview:
Oxandrolone, known as Anavar, is an oral anabolic steroid once used medically for weight recovery and used by some for physique goals, including by women.

Its article lists voice deepening and other virilizing effects in women, some of which can be irreversible.
quick.mechanism: It is an androgen receptor agonist described as strongly anabolic with weak androgenic action; virilization still occurs.
quick.risks: Documented risks include liver damage, lipid changes, virilization in women, pregnancy contraindication, drug interactions, and controlled-substance status.

lead: Oxandrolone, sold as Oxandrin and widely known as Anavar or 'Var', is an oral anabolic-androgenic steroid. In physique circles it is valued for lean-muscle gain and for use during fat-loss phases, and it has a reputation as one of the milder steroids, partly because it has strong anabolic and weak androgenic effects in rodent studies [1]. Wikipedia states that it has about 5 percent of testosterone's androgenic potency and up to six times its anabolic potency in those measurements [1]. That reputation is the reason women and first-time users have often chosen it, and it is why its voice and virilization risks are a frequent topic.

Medically, it has been used to promote weight gain after surgery, trauma or chronic illness, to counter muscle loss from long-term corticosteroids, and to aid recovery from severe burns, where reviews report more lean mass and faster donor-site healing [1][2]. Those same lean-mass effects are what bodybuilders and athletes seek for a harder, leaner physique [1][3].

In women, documented androgenic effects include voice deepening, body and facial hair growth, menstrual changes, male-pattern hair loss and clitoral enlargement, and the voice and other virilizing changes can be irreversible [1][12]. A 1989 survey of competitive bodybuilders in Kansas and Missouri found Anavar among the steroids reported by female competitors [4]. The US Food and Drug Administration formally withdrew approval for all oxandrolone indications in 2023 [1].

chain: Oral anabolic steroid with strong anabolic activity
Promotes lean mass and retention during dieting
Harder, leaner physique; voice and virilization risk in women
angle.text: People use oxandrolone to add or keep lean muscle while dieting, for a leaner, more muscular look. Its reputation as relatively mild is why it is popular with women, although virilizing effects, including voice deepening that can persist, are documented [1].

infobox: US Schedule III; Canada Schedule IV; UK Schedule 4 [1]

paras: People who use oxandrolone for physique goals seek lean mass with limited water retention during a diet, a firmer-looking body and, for some, a visible reduction in the look of fat. Bodybuilders and athletes have used it non-medically for muscle building, and it has appeared in professional doping cases [1]. It is popular with women and with people seeking milder steroid regimens, which Wikipedia attributes to its higher anabolic-to-androgenic ratio and a reputation for lower liver toxicity that later proved mistaken [1]. A 1989 survey of competitive bodybuilders found it among the steroids named by both men and women, with the main reason for steroid use being the perception that they helped win competitions [4].

Labeled and off-label uses include weight gain after surgery, trauma, chronic infection or HIV wasting, countering corticosteroid-related muscle breakdown, and bone pain in osteoporosis [1]. A 2022 systematic review of six randomized trials found a skin-healing advantage with oxandrolone as an adjunct in adult burn patients and no benefit in pressure ulcers [2]. Wikipedia reports reduced catabolic weight loss, greater lean body mass, better donor-site healing and shorter intensive-care and hospital stays in burn patients, thought to reflect a lower hypermetabolic response [1]. A 2019 Cochrane review, as described on Wikipedia, found moderate-quality evidence that adding it to growth hormone increased adult height in girls with Turner syndrome, although growth hormone had largely replaced oxandrolone for this use by 2015 [1].

Virilization means the development of adult male characteristics in females and is driven by androgens. Wikipedia lists deepening of the voice, clitoral enlargement, increased muscle strength, acne, excess body hair, frontal hair thinning, menstrual disruption and increased libido among its signs; it lists voice deepening, facial and body hair growth, male-pattern baldness and clitoral enlargement as permanent, while extra upper-body muscle, sweating and lipid changes are listed as reversible [11].

For oxandrolone specifically, Wikipedia says irreversible masculinizing effects may occur in women, including voice deepening, hirsutism, menstrual abnormalities, male-pattern hair loss and clitoral enlargement, and notes that doses for women and children are kept as low as possible with monitoring for virilization [1]. The more general article on anabolic steroids states that voice deepening from these drugs in women is irreversible, together with hirsutism, menstrual disturbances and breast and uterine atrophy [12].

Wikipedia's history of female bodybuilding records that in 1992 the IFBB introduced femininity rules after concern about size and 'androgenic side effects' among competitors, and in 2004 an IFBB memo asked female athletes to reduce muscularity [13].

Liver enzymes can rise, especially at high doses or prolonged use, and peliosis hepatis, liver failure and liver tumors have been documented; the early belief that it was far less liver-toxic than other oral steroids did not hold up [1]. The FDA withdrawal described by Wikipedia cited peliosis hepatis, liver cell tumors, adverse blood lipid changes, cholestatic hepatitis, hypercalcemia in breast cancer patients and prostate concerns in older patients [1]. It alters blood lipids, can reduce male fertility, strongly potentiates warfarin (the manufacturer issued a safety alert in April 2004) and is contraindicated in pregnancy [1]. A 1991 report described gynecomastia in 33 adolescent boys treated for short stature [1]. A 2020 case report described delayed rhabdomyolysis after a man used Anavar for 60 consecutive days [5].

More broadly, Wikipedia's anabolic steroid article describes cardiovascular effects (cholesterol changes, hypertension, left ventricular hypertrophy), kidney findings, a Group 2A 'probably carcinogenic' listing by the IARC and psychiatric effects such as aggression and dependence across the drug class [12].

Oxandrolone is a 17-alpha-methylated derivative of dihydrotestosterone with an oxygen atom replacing carbon 2 (chemical name 2-oxa-17alpha-methyl-DHT). It is an androgen receptor agonist with strong anabolic and weak androgenic effects in rodents, and it does not convert to estrogens, so gynecomastia is generally not expected from the drug's own pharmacology [1]. The anabolic-to-androgenic ratio is measured in rodents with a protocol dating to the 1950s based on prostate and levator ani muscle weights; Wikipedia notes that in humans all anabolic steroids have significant androgenic effects, so the separation seen in animals is less marked [12]. Wikipedia still documents virilization in women [1].

Oral bioavailability is about 97 percent and plasma protein binding 94 to 97 percent. Wikipedia states it is metabolized mainly by the kidneys and less by the liver, unusual among oral anabolic steroids, with an elimination half-life of about 9.4 to 10.4 hours in adults and 13.3 hours in the elderly; about 28 percent of an oral dose is excreted unchanged in urine and 3 percent in feces [1].

Oxandrolone is a synthetic androstane steroid with the formula C19H30O3 and a molar mass of about 306 g/mol. It is related to mestanolone, oxymetholone and stanozolol [1]. Its crystal structure, with that of other 2-oxa-steroids, has been described in crystallography work [8].

Raphael Pappo and Christopher J. Jung at Searle Laboratories first made and described oxandrolone in 1962, and it entered US medical use in 1964 [1]. A 1984 FDA advisory committee unanimously concluded there was no evidence of efficacy for the drug's labeled uses [1]. Searle discontinued Anavar in 1989, partly because of bad publicity from illicit bodybuilding use, and Savient (formerly Bio-Technology General) launched Oxandrin in 1995 after successful trials [1].

In April 2004 Savient issued an FDA safety alert about oxandrolone's strong interaction with warfarin, and by 2011 the drug held US orphan designations for alcoholic hepatitis, Turner syndrome and HIV-related weight loss [1]. Gemini asked the FDA to withdraw approval on 26 March 2019, stating it no longer marketed the drug; the FDA notified license holders on 16 December 2022 that it should be removed from the market, and approval for all indications was formally withdrawn in June 2023, with a further Federal Register determination in September 2023 that Oxandrin tablets were withdrawn for safety or effectiveness reasons [1]. As of August 2023, Wikipedia lists the remaining US medical options for anabolic steroids as testosterone and its esters, methyltestosterone, fluoxymesterone and oxymetholone [1].

Brand names include Anavar (the original brand, marketed in the US and the Netherlands), Oxandrin (the US brand after Anavar and the sole US brand as of 2011), Antitriol (Spain), Anatrophill (France), Lipidex (Brazil), Lonavar (Argentina, Australia, Italy), Protivar and Vasorome (Japan). 'Var' is a colloquial name among non-medical users [1].

Wikipedia lists oxandrolone as a US Schedule III controlled substance, Schedule IV in Canada (as of 2017), Schedule 4 in the UK (as of 2017) and Class C5 in Brazil. It is no longer available in Europe and remains available in some less-regulated markets such as Malaysia and Mexico [1]. Where anabolic steroids are controlled, Wikipedia notes a black market exists that includes smuggled, clandestinely made and counterfeit products [12].

Bodybuilders and athletes have used oxandrolone illicitly, and cases involving professional athletes are listed under doping in sport [1]. A survey of 466 male gym attendees in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia (conducted 2024 to 2025) examined the prevalence and awareness of anabolic-androgenic steroid use, comparing gym users with non-users [3]. A 1989 survey found 54 percent of male competitive bodybuilders and 10 percent of female competitors in Kansas and Missouri were regular steroid users [4]. Wikipedia estimates that 1 to 3 million people in the United States have used anabolic steroids, most of them noncompetitive bodybuilders or non-athletes [12].

Looksmax.org has threads on Anavar for cutting and for height. One poster planning use in his mid-teens cites pediatric growth studies and says he wants to address a delayed bone age [6]. Other posters in those discussions say it affects natural hormone production and should not be run alone [6]. Another thread describes it as great for cutting [7], and a comparison thread sets it against another steroid [10]. A thread by a 14-year-old asking about oxandrolone with growth hormone drew replies that were encouraging; the wiki records these as community discussion and does not reproduce dosing, cycle or sourcing details [9].

No studies found on oxandrolone and voice change in women specifically. Studies of the drug cover burns [2], pressure ulcers [2] and Turner syndrome [1], and a 2019 case report documents delayed rhabdomyolysis after anabolic-androgenic steroid use [5].

timeline.event: Described by Searle chemists Raphael Pappo and Christopher Jung [1].
An FDA advisory committee unanimously finds no evidence of efficacy for labeled uses [1].
Searle discontinues Anavar; a survey of bodybuilders in Kansas and Missouri is published [1][4].
The IFBB introduces femininity rules for women's bodybuilding citing androgenic side effects [13].
Manufacturer issues an FDA safety alert on the warfarin interaction [1].
Gemini asks the FDA to withdraw approval (26 March) [1].
FDA notifies license holders the drug should be removed from the market (16 December) [1].
FDA formally withdraws approval for all indications [1].

lore.intro: On looksmax.org Anavar is discussed as a cutting aid, as a perceived mild steroid for women, and, by younger posters, as a possible tool for height [6][7].

claims.claim: Anavar can add height in teens with open growth plates.
claims.believers: A poster cites pediatric growth studies from the 1980s and 1990s reporting faster growth velocity in boys given oxandrolone and plans to use it for height [6].
claims.experts: Wikipedia describes use in Turner syndrome with growth hormone and notes growth hormone has largely replaced it; the effect on adult height in otherwise healthy teens is not established in the sources cited here [1].

claims.believers: A looksmax.org thread describes it as useful for lean-out phases [7].
claims.experts: Medical studies show it reduces catabolic weight loss and increases lean mass in burn patients [1][2]; its use for physique cutting is non-medical.

claims.claim: Anavar is mild and low-risk for women.
claims.believers: Users cite its low androgenic rating and the reputation for lower liver toxicity [1].
claims.experts: Reference sources document voice deepening, hirsutism, menstrual changes and clitoral enlargement that can be irreversible, and liver toxicity in some users [1][11][12].

claims.claim: Anavar can be used by teenagers aiming for extra height
claims.believers: A 14-year-old on looksmax.org described asking about oxandrolone with growth hormone to maximize his remaining year of growth, and respondents replied with suggestions for combining compounds [9]. Another thread cites pediatric growth studies and delayed bone age as the rationale [6].
claims.experts: Pediatric growth research on oxandrolone concerns clinically supervised conditions such as Turner syndrome combined with growth hormone [1]. No study has tested oxandrolone for increasing height in otherwise healthy teens.

claims.claim: It must be used with a testosterone base to avoid hormone problems
claims.believers: Respondents on looksmax.org said oxandrolone alone suppresses natural hormones and should be accompanied by testosterone [6].
claims.experts: Anabolic-androgenic steroids as a class are known to suppress the body's own testosterone production; Wikipedia describes oxandrolone's effect on male fertility [1].
